item.title: Jewel Perez receives 20 years for shootout with Lubbock authorities
item.description: Jewel Perez was sentenced to 10 years in the Texas Department of Criminal Justice after violating her probation and 20 years for Aggravated Assault with a Deadly Weapon, after a 2023 incident where she got into a shootout with Lubbock authorities. Her sentence will be served concurrently.

item.title: TTUHSC student converts elementary school into a mosque
item.description: Within the span of 45 days, Texas Tech Health Science Center medical student was able to turn a former elementary school into a place where the community can gather.

item.title: New Home moms oppose special education classroom relocation to O'Donnell
item.description: New Home families who have a child in the Life skills classroom are upset at the recent decision made by New Home Independent School District board about a vote to move its program to O'Donnell ISD for the next school year, which is over 30 miles away.

item.title: Lubbock Feeders announces feedyard closure after 70 years
item.description: It’s the end of an era on the South Plains. After 70 years of operation, Lubbock Feeders, a cornerstone of the region’s agricultural economy since 1955, has announced it will close its doors.
